title: Custom ClientRegistrationRepository conflicts with OAuth2 client auto-configuration, OAuth2ClientProperties not available: exclude the auto-configuration
errorSample:
Caused by: org.springframework.beans.factory.NoSuchBeanDefinitionException: No qualifying bean of type 'org.springframework.boot.security.oauth2.client.autoconfigure.OAuth2ClientProperties' available: expected at least 1 bean which qualifies as autowire candidate. Dependency annotations: {}
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.DefaultListableBeanFactory.raiseNoMatchingBeanFound(DefaultListableBeanFactory.java:2304) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.DefaultListableBeanFactory.doResolveDependency(DefaultListableBeanFactory.java:1732) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.DefaultListableBeanFactory.resolveDependency(DefaultListableBeanFactory.java:1658) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.ConstructorResolver.resolveAutowiredArgument(ConstructorResolver.java:912) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.ConstructorResolver.createArgumentArray(ConstructorResolver.java:791) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	... 122 common frames omitted
symptom: Context startup fails with NoSuchBeanDefinitionException for OAuth2ClientProperties in a configuration that defines its own ClientRegistrationRepository bean and has spring.security.oauth2.client.registration.* set.
cause: Two competing definitions of the client registration infrastructure are active at once: the auto-configured one and the user-defined repository. The auto-configuration's partial registration leaves the properties bean in a half-initialized state that cannot be injected.
fixSummary: Exclude the OAuth2 client auto-configuration so the user-defined repository is the only definition: spring.autoconfigure.exclude=org.springframework.boot.security.oauth2.client.autoconfigure.OAuth2ClientAutoConfiguration in application.properties. The conflict disappears and the custom repository bean receives its dependencies.
